text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — elevated 502/504 ratio detected from prod-gateway in us-west-2. error-rate up 4.8% over baseline in last 3m. auto-escalation: P1. See /incidents/3987654321

ayush: acked, oncall. jumping in. can someone post customer impact (which endpoints/users)?

sarah: seeing spike on /v1/generate and /v1/chat with timeouts propagated from upstream model pool. 95th latency also up. sample: 502s with grpc upstream closed stream.

mike: I can see surge in connections hitting gateway-worker-12/13; backend pool for gpt-medium is hitting OOM-ish evictions then 504s. logs for those hosts are mostly empty around the failures.

julia: heads up — observability shows many requests missing span ids. traces are sparse; most sampled traces absent. looks like trace sampler got flipped to 0.01 accidentally in last deploy.

ayush: ouch. who's on the deploy that changed sampler?

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-15_09:12 by jules to service:telemetry-agent — config set 'trace-sampling-rate' = 0.01 (was 0.1).

julia: yep that explains the darkness. we need immediate temporary instrumentation to recover visibility while mitigating customer impact.

sarah: mitigation plan proposal:
- roll sampler back to 0.1 (or 0.2) on telemetry-agent (hotfix)
- enable request-level debug logging for gateway-worker group for 10m
- add temporary log-forwarder bypass to capture stderr for evicted hosts
- if backend pool unstable, route traffic to gpt-small fallback for non-critical routes

mike: rolling sampler rollback now (hotpatch). running:

```
kubectl set env ds/telemetry-agent TRACE_SAMPLING=0.15 -n infra-production
kubectl rollout restart ds/telemetry-agent -n infra-production
```

mike: applied. telemetry agents rolling, should see sample rate climb in ~30s.

ayush: enabling debug logs on gateway-workers for 15m. command:

```
ssh ops@promoter
for node in gw-*-worker-12 gw-*-worker-13; do sudo systemctl set-log-level redwood-gateway debug; done
```

ops-bot: Debug logging enabled on gw-worker-12/13 for 15m (expires 2026-03-15T09:35Z).

julia: I also pushed a temporary trace proxy that forces add span-id header when missing. snippet used in prod-obs:

```
if not request.headers.get('X-Span-Id'):
  request.headers['X-Span-Id'] = uuid4()
```

sarah: good quick hack. also started a small traffic shift: 8% to fallback gpt-small via routing rule. watching errors and latency.

mike: noticed logs being backfilled now — we have stack traces for a few evictions. appears a memory leak in model server under certain prompt lengths (tokens > 2048). reproducing locally.

ayush: customer impact estimate: ~2.1% of requests got 5xx in the last 10m, affecting ~1100 active users, mostly interactive chat sessions. CS notified.

julia: important: we still lack request body samples for many hits due to redaction + sampling. enabling a targeted capture for requests with status>=500 for 200 requests max.

sarah: added small capture rule in ingress to stash up to 200 failing payloads into secure-bucket (encrypted) for 1h. command:

```
redwoodctl capture create --filter 'status>=500' --limit 200 --dest s3://incident-captures/3987654321
```

mike: while reproducing, found model-server crash when kv-cache pressure + long seq. pushing small patch to server that avoids prefetch when mem > 80%.

ayush: can we hotfix model fleet or do we need to rollback recent model build? what's safer?

mike: patch is small and tested on canary. deploying to 10% of model pool as staged rollback. if green, promote.

ops-bot: routing shift metrics: fallback gpt-small latency + p95 increased by 40ms, error-rate on primary pool decreasing.

sarah: good. once telemetry agents finish rolling we should see traces reappear; anyone seeing spans yet?

julia: few traces showing up, span-ids present for sampled failures. able to correlate to model instance ids.

ayush: customer comms: CS posted initial note to affected customers (template A). we'll escalate if degradation persists >30m.

mike: can confirm model-server patch on 10% is stable so far (10m). promoting to 50% now.

sarah: monitoring: keep an eye on OOMs, connection resets, and any increase in 429s due to routing. ops — please keep debug logs active until we have stable telemetry.

ops-bot: debug logs extended by 10m.

julia: follow-ups / post-incident tasks:
- revert debug logging change after incident
- harden telemetry deploy gating to avoid accidental sampler flips
- add alert for rapid drop in trace volume
- add targeted unit/regression tests for long sequences causing memory pressure
- review log redaction rules that prevented some request bodies from being captured

ayush: agreed. I'm going to start a postmortem doc and hand this to SRE rotation. handing off to sarah for triage & epic.

sarah: taking over. thanks team. will update postmortem doc and link backlog tickets. closing the active page once metrics stable for 10m.

incident-bot: Incident 3987654321 status: mitigated -> monitoring. severity lowered to P2. next update in 10m or on ask.

mike: final note — root cause appears to be interplay of reduced trace sampling (visibility gap) + model-server memory regression on long sequences. mitigations: rollback sampler, hotpatch model server, temporary routing. will prepare RCA.

ayush: thanks all. great coordination. :thumbsup:
